memos.risk:
Risk officer view on CODE (MintMyCode):

Classification: the brief says ORGANIC, but the curve data points the other way. A bundle share of 84.7% on the bonding curve suggests coordinated buying, and the first two minutes after graduation show a launch bot and a sell-to-buy ratio above 1. The 62% last-15-minute return with heavy selling (220 sellers against 254 buyers) looks like late distribution. I'd downgrade this from ORGANIC before sizing.

If the desk buys anyway: ticket $5, not $20. Stop at 20%, since the drawdown from the 30-minute high is already 3%. Hold no longer than 15 minutes.

Refuse entirely if the bundle share is not explained, if pool depth stays near 100 SOL (a $20 round trip faces heavy impact), or if net flow turns negative. Skipping costs nothing; I'd skip.
memos.scout:
Case for buying CODE now, at most honest reading:

Demand looks broad rather than concentrated. Last 15 minutes: 254 buyers and 220 sellers, with 110.6 SOL bought against 86.2 SOL sold, so net inflow of 24.4 SOL. Top-3 holder share is only 10.3%, and the top-5 buyer share in the first two minutes after graduation was 19.5%. The 30-minute high drawdown is just 3.1%, and the coin is up 45% over 30 minutes and 62% over 15. It is not an airdrop factory, so that failure mode is absent.

Against that, the case is weak. The curve shows 84.7% bundle share, a launch bot was present, and sells slightly exceeded buys (ratio 1.13) right after graduation. A pool of 102.7 SOL means a $20 ticket moves price, and a round trip costs 1.4-5.1%. Net inflow over 15 minutes is modest, and the 30-minute window sits in the range where random buys have lost about 20%.

Verdict: the case for buying is thin. The positive signals are real but the bundling and bot presence are exactly what the base rates penalize. I would not buy this now. Skipping costs nothing.
memos.skeptic: The most likely loss path is insider distribution into the recent rally. The curve shows bundle_share at 0.85 and completer_share at 0.27, so most early supply was bought in bundles, probably by a few operators who could sell into retail demand. Over the last 15 minutes, sell_sol (86.2) nearly matched buy_sol (110.6), with 220 sellers against 254 buyers, so the price is being absorbed by heavy two-way churn rather than steady accumulation. The launch bot present and the sell-to-buy ratio of 1.13 in the first two minutes after graduation point the same way. With a 0.62 return over 15 minutes and only 2.9% off the 30-minute high, a reversal would start quickly. At a 102.7 SOL pool, a 2-5% round trip cost is a large share of any move this coin can plausibly make in an hour. Skip.
